messages:
Marta: Hey folks, saw a spike of persistent 429s in eu-west yesterday ~03:10 UTC. Not a single burst — looks like clients keep probing and connections stay hot, which blocked admissions.
Devin: Yep. New customer with wide context + streaming. When GPUs saturated those probe heartbeats became a thundering herd.
Raj: Traces show probes tagged with header `X-Redwood-Client-Probe: 1` coming every 1s and no exponential backoff. We temporarily rate-limited probes at the edge.
Emily: Can we standardize an admit/window header so SDKs can pace properly? e.g. `X-Admit-Window-ms: 1200` and `X-Admit-Expires: 1742005000` (epoch ttl).
Marta: Exactly. If the response carries an admit window + expires, SDKs should suppress probe traffic until TTL or reduce rate. Also include a policy header like `X-Admit-Policy: suspend|probe-slow|best-effort`.
Devin: Also recommend SDK change: exponential backoff with jitter for probes. Pseudocode: `backoff = base_ms * 2^retries * (0.8 + rand()*0.4)`, cap to 30s.
sre-bot: ALERT #INC-4123 created: eu-west gpu-pool saturated, autoscaler at max.
Raj: Quick mitigation rolled: cap probes to 1 per 10s per client connection and honor `X-Admit-Expires`. Canary deployed to eu-west now.
Emily: For streaming use-cases we need different semantics — streaming connections poll lighter but frequently. We should avoid killing streams.
SDK-Team: Proposal: add `X-Stream-Intent: 1` on upfront request. Streaming requests go through a separate low-cost admission queue. If rejected, return 425 (early hint) so SDK can buffer then retry with backoff instead of hammering with probes.
Devin: 425 vs 429 — we get into semantics. 425 cleanly signals client-side buffering, but existing SDKs treat 429 as the universal throttle. Need coordinated SDK+server change.
Marta: Note for Product: probes during saturation doubled token-level cost last night since each probe triggered expensive kernel warmups. We should include cost impact in customer comms.
Emily: I'll open a docs PR explaining new headers + recommended SDK backoff and flag support windows.
Raj: After canary, we'll emit `X-Admit-Window-ms` and `X-Admit-Expires` on overload responses and add metric `admit.window.ms` and `admit.suppressed_probes`.
Marta: Action items: (1) SDK-Team: honor admit headers + implement exponential backoff w/ jitter and stream intent handling; (2) Raj: canary probe cap and emit headers from overload path; (3) Emily: docs + customer note. I'll follow up in #eng-platform with rollout timeline. :thumbsup:
SDK-Team: We'll aim for an SDK patch in the next minor release and include a config knob `admit_behavior: "honor-server" | "legacy"`.
Marta: Thanks — keeping this thread for the rollouts.
